_about: What's new in each LFG release, said to the user: the walkthrough the dashboard shows once after an update, Help → What's new, and the lines `lfg setup` prints. Each item is one step of the walkthrough: page and sel (optional) say which page to open and what to light up on it. Newest release first. CHANGELOG.md keeps the detailed record.

items.title: Groups can hold groups, and studios can join them
items.text: Group your sessions as an epic, then its milestones, then sessions, and put Studio chats in the same groups. Add colour labels to cut across them, and let a group follow a ticket so its sessions join on their own.

items.title: Re-reviews show what changed
items.text: A re-review now starts with what was fixed, what is new and what is still open. Fixed findings are crossed out with the points they gave back, and you can copy all new findings, all still-open findings or all questions for an agent in one click.

releases.title: Ask the PR's author, and every tab updates

items.title: Ask the PR's author
items.text: When a review has a question only the PR's author can answer, press Ask the author on GitHub under it. It's posted on the line it's about, their reply shows under the question, and Use their reply as the answer lets the review update itself. Re-reviews read their replies too.

items.title: Every open tab gets the update
items.text: When you update LFG, every dashboard tab you have open now switches to the new version by itself, not just the one you clicked Update in.

releases.title: Browser tabs say where you are

items.title: Browser tabs say where you are
items.text: Each dashboard tab in your browser now shows the repo, the page and what's open, shortened: for example "ext · PRs · #1800" or "aegis · Studio · Fix the export". Switching repos updates it.

releases.title: Tabs follow your repo, and message times

items.title: Tabs follow your repo
items.text: The Studio and PR review tabs in the sidebar and above the page now change with the repo you pick top left, so each repo shows its own sessions and PRs.

items.title: Plugins from your claude.ai account
items.text: Integrations → Claude Code plugins now says when a plugin comes from your claude.ai account or organisation, and that you change it there, instead of calling it a one-repo install.

items.title: When each message was sent
items.text: Every message in Studio and in a PR review's chat, yours and Claude's, shows when it was sent: the time for today, the date and time for earlier days. Hover it for the full date.

releases.title: Corrections, tabs, review combos and plugins

items.title: Corrections
items.text: When you correct Claude ("no, use pnpm", a tool call you reject, or a correction that's more a feeling than a no), LFG can queue it here. You decide what becomes a rule; nothing does without you. It's off until you switch it on here, then click Install once.

items.title: Rules with a why and an example
items.text: Approve a correction as a rule for every repo or only the one it was said in. Add why it matters and a real time it went wrong: Claude is told both with the rule. Each rule has its own switch, and LFG points out a rule you already have that says much the same, so you can merge instead of adding another.

items.title: Or keep it in your second-brain
items.text: Some corrections are background about you rather than how Claude should work. Save to second-brain keeps those as a note Claude looks up when it matters, instead of telling every session.

items.title: Studio sessions open as tabs
items.text: Every session you open becomes a tab, above the session and at the top of Studio in the sidebar, with a dot that shows whether it's working, waiting or needs you. Drag a tab in either place to reorder.

items.title: Pin a tab
items.text: Hover a tab, in PR reviews or Studio, and click the pin to keep it at the front. Pinned tabs have no close button and are never dropped when you have many open. Drag a tab among the pinned ones to pin it, or out of them to unpin it.

items.title: The setup guide can be skipped
items.text: The guide that opens the first time you use the dashboard now has a Skip button, and Escape closes it. The ⓘ button in the top bar opens it again.

items.title: Review combos, and plugin review skills
items.text: The review Method picker now lists review skills from plugins you installed, such as superpowers. Tick the methods you want together and click Save as combo to name the set; one click picks a combo, and the star makes one your default.

items.title: Claude Code plugins, from LFG
items.text: Integrations now lists your Claude Code plugins, each with an on/off switch that keeps it installed, and Remove. Search the marketplaces and install one, such as superpowers, without the terminal. Claude can't install plugins on its own any more: only you can.

items.title: What's new, after every update
items.text: Updates now come as numbered releases rather than every change, and this walkthrough shows once after each one. Help → What's new lists every release and replays any of them. Settings → General → Updates switches back to every change if you prefer.

items.title: LFG Dictate
items.text: Hold Option+Space anywhere on your Mac to dictate, on-device. Off until you turn it on: `lfg add dictate`. Open `lfg ui` for a 1-minute tour.

items.title: Experimental labels
items.text: Pentest and Headroom are now labelled Experimental.
